newsitem.title: INDIA: Posters in Srinagar seek clues on Western hostages.
newsitem.headline: Posters in Srinagar seek clues on Western hostages.

text.p: Indian police on Saturday pasted posters on the walls of troubled Kashmir's biggest city, offering a one million rupee ($28,000) reward for information on four Westerners taken hostage 17 months ago.

The posters in Srinagar, summer capital of the state of Jammu and Kashmir, carried pictures of American Donald Hutchings, German Dirk Hasert and Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells, kidnapped by shadowy Al-Faran guerrillas in July 1995.
The reward was announced on Thursday.

"We have already sent several police parties for pasting and distributing these posters across the valley, but our main concern will be Doda and south Kashmir regions," Mohammad Amin Shah, head of a team probing the abductions, told Reuters.
The hilly district of Doda is a guerrilla stronghold in southern Kashmir where the four Westerners were abducted on a Himalayan trek.
One other hostage, American John Childs, escaped while a sixth, Hans Christian Ostroe of Norway, was found beheaded in August 1995.
"Soon, through radio, television and local newspapers, we will publicise this reward," Shah said.

Dozens of Moslem guerrilla groups have been fighting New Delhi's rule in the state, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province. More than 20,000 people have died in violence linked to a rebellion that broke out in 1990.
